commits.message:
perf(text): fold spans into pieces instead of rescanning them (rich-text-6po) (#110)

`RichText._buildSegments` cut the text at every span edge and then asked, of
every piece, which of *all* the spans covered it. The pieces are cut by the
spans, so that charged `spans x pieces` — the square of the span count — and
anything styling densely reached it in ordinary use: a `ReprHighlighter` over a
large value, `highlightRegex` over a common character, `Pretty`'s indent guides.

Walk it span-first instead. A span covers a piece exactly when it covers the
piece's first character, because the pieces are cut at the span edges, so each
span owns one contiguous run of pieces and can be written into it once. Every
span edge is already a boundary, which makes the run's opening a map lookup
rather than a search.

Span-first also keeps the composition honest for free: `Style.add` is
order-dependent and the last writer wins, so the styles have to fold in
`_spans` order — which iterating `_spans` is, and which a position-ordered
sweep would have had to reconstruct.

Two dead guards went with it. Neither the empty-text early return nor the
empty-piece `continue` could fire: the boundaries come from a Set, so
consecutive ones always differ, and zero-length text produces no pieces at all.
A span covering nothing — empty, reversed, or past the text — still cuts the
text where its edges land, as before, and now folds into an empty run rather
than into a case.

Measured against eb9a18e7, same machine:

                                        before      after
  8,000 one-character spans             833.5ms      7.6ms
  4,000                                  62.7ms      4.8ms
  1,000                                  15.1ms      3.7ms
  Pretty nest(200), guides on          7081.0ms     82.8ms
  Pretty nest(100), guides on           758.1ms     25.5ms
  ReprHighlighter, 1,600 spans           61.2ms      4.0ms
  Pretty nest(1000), guides off         355.9ms    345.8ms

The last row is the control: guides off was never span-dense, so it is the row
that should not move, and it doesn't.

Output is unchanged. 2,798 renders — base styles, overlapping and identically
ranged spans in both orders, empty/reversed/out-of-range spans, all four
justifications with and without wrap, three highlighters, `Pretty` with guides
on and off, and the slice/divide/truncate paths — are byte-identical to
eb9a18e7.

The regression test counts span-bound reads rather than milliseconds, the way
`pretty.test.ts` counts getter reads: a wrong version still looks fast at any
input small enough to keep a test quick. It asserts the ratio between two sizes
so no constant has to stay true — 400 to 800 spans doubles the reads now and
quadrupled them before (241k -> 962k).

`pretty.test.ts`'s thousand-level render now runs at default options, with the
indent guides it had to disable to arrive. That is rich-pretty-51c's done-when,
which this unblocks.
